items.item: Server is the only writer of Gold; client never sends amounts or prices
Validates remote arguments (types, NaN/inf, bounds) and rate-limits shop requests
Avoids yields between balance check and deduction (atomic spend)
Persistence handled safely (UpdateAsync or session-locked profile; load-before-play; BindToClose)
Does not treat leaderstats as source of truth
Kill rewards awarded by server-side kill attribution, not a client 'I killed X' remote

slop: Calls ProfileStore 'loadstring-free', a label that adds nothing

incorrect_or_stale: Says Roblox has a built-in remote throttle of 'about 500 requests/s'; this is unverified and likely wrong
slop: Header '*Apex: security → data → networking*' is noise

raw.reason: Both are equally secure and use the same architecture (session-locked ProfileStore, a single Gold writer, atomic TrySpend, server-derived rewards). A also supports stackable items, while B gives clearer kill-attribution caveats and test steps, so neither is clearly better.
